in_greek.name: Νταρύλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Νταρύλ είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'αγαπητός' ή 'εκτιμητός'. Το όνομα Νταρύλ πιθανότατα συνδέεται με τη λέξη 'δάρυς' που σημαίνει 'δάσος' ή 'ξύλο'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Νταρύλ δεν αναφέρεται ρητά, αλλά η έννοια της αγάπης και της εκτίμησης είναι κεντρική στη διδασκαλία του Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Daryle
in_latin.long_meaning: Daryle is a name derived from Latin roots, signifying 'beloved' or 'dearly loved'. The name Daryle is likely connected to the Latin word 'carus,' meaning 'dear' or 'beloved.' in_english.name: Daryle
in_english.long_meaning: Daryle is a Christian name that originated from Hebrew and Greek roots, signifying 'beloved' or 'dearly loved.' The name Daryle is likely derived from the Hebrew word 'dor,' meaning 'gift' or 'generation,' and the Greek word 'daru,' meaning 'to give.' In Christian tradition, the name Daryle reflects the idea of being a beloved child of God, cherished and loved. Historically, the name Daryle has been used across various Christian cultures, symbolizing spiritual significance and divine love.

data.cultural_impact: Daryle, being derived from the Greek name 'dareios', carries a cultural significance associated with the sea or fish. Historically, fish was a prominent symbol in early Christian communities as seen in various scriptures such as Matthew 4:19 where Jesus called four fishermen to be his disciples; the miraculous feeding of the multitude with loaves and fishes (Mark 6:30-44), and Saint Peter, one of the twelve apostles and leader of the early Church, who was a fisherman by trade. Through this association, names like Daryle carry a rich heritage representing the early Christian fishing communities and the teachings of Jesus.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Daryle, derived from the Greek word 'dareios', also holds a significant spiritual meaning as it reminds us of the Biblical figure Darius, a Median king mentioned in the Old and New Testaments, who was converted to Christianity (possibly under Bishop Paul of Samosata, according to the authors of the Church History of Eusebius). This name serves as a testament to the power of God in bringing people from all walks of life to the saving grace of faith, and is a reminder to remain open to the divine guidance and transformation.
